# The wrapper also rewrites the standard library: encoding/asn1 negates big
# integers with "bytes[i] ^= 0xff", which is vectorized while the program's
# output stays the same.

exec go run .
cmp stdout want.out

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=encoding/asn1
exec go build -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
! stdout .
! stderr .
cmp log log.want

exec ./app
cmp stdout want.out

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"encoding/asn1"
	"fmt"
	"math/big"
)

func main() {
	for _, n := range []int64{-300, -1, -65536, 300} {
		der, err := asn1.Marshal(big.NewInt(n))
		fmt.Println(n, der, err)
	}
}
-- want.out --
-300 [2 2 254 212] <nil>
-1 [2 1 255] <nil>
-65536 [2 3 255 0 0] <nil>
300 [2 2 1 44] <nil>
-- log.want --
rewrote 2 loop(s) in encoding/asn1
